chapter: Influences, Los Angeles scene and technique
title: Elmo Hope and the Hillcrest versus West Coast jazz
summary: Elmo Hope and Harold Land writing together and how the Hillcrest differed from white West Coast jazz.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Elmo – I used to go – Harold Land used to be over there a lot. Harold and Elmo used to write a lot of stuff, really unbelievable, intricate things. Elmo, he was something. A lot of people didn’t know about him. As you really looked what was going on in New York, an awful lot of musicians that are in New York came from L.A. They used to have this thing. They used to talk about West Coast Jazz. That was – that was Shorty Rogers. It wasn’t at the Hillcrest. What was happening at the Hillcrest, it was very ethnic.
Where was it located, the Hillcrest?
On Washington Boulevard. It was very heavy.
So what I hear you saying, there were two different scenes on the West Coast.
